title: US Treasury sell-off deepens, 10-year yield hits 19-year high post-Fed hike
content:
The bond-market rout that followed the Fed's first rate hike since 2023 intensified through the week, with the 10-year US Treasury yield jumping to **5.22%** on 24 September 2026, its highest since 2007, and the 30-year touching 5.50%, a level last seen in 2004. The Fed had raised its target range by 25bp to **3.75%-4.00%** on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote, with Chair Kevin Warsh warning that underlying inflation remains too high.

Traders priced better than a **75%** chance of a further hike in October, and stronger-than-expected economic data and high oil prices added to selling pressure across the curve. Higher borrowing costs weighed on rate-sensitive sectors, though equities largely shrugged off the move on the week.

title: Brent eases from war highs as Iran floats Strait of Hormuz reopening
content:
Brent crude, which had spiked above **$100/bbl** earlier in September after US-Iran strikes hit Saudi Aramco infrastructure, fell **2.1%** to settle near **$104/bbl** on 25 September 2026. The drop followed a proposal from Iran's foreign minister to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks within seven days, in exchange for the US lifting its naval blockade and unfreezing Iranian assets.

The pullback offered some relief on the inflation front that had complicated the Fed's rate decision earlier in the week, though traders cautioned gains could reverse quickly given the fragility of the talks and the risk of renewed attacks on regional energy infrastructure.

title: Wall Street ends winning week as AI rally offsets bond-yield surge
content:
US equities snapped a two-week losing run as an AI-led rally overshadowed the bond sell-off. The Dow rose **478** points, or **0.9%**, on Friday to 51,828.62, while the S&P 500 added 0.5% to 7,743.41 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.5% to a record 27,068.72 on 25 September 2026, led by megacap technology names.

The Russell 2000 fell on the week even as large-cap benchmarks notched their first weekly gain in three, underscoring a narrow, megacap-led advance. Investors flagged the divergence as a risk, with the 10-year Treasury yield hovering near **5.2%**, its highest in nearly two decades.
